description: Eight fictional study abstracts for a RAG coding assessment. These are not real clinical evidence. Keep them separate from live web results.
usage: Embed the abstract text and retain record_id, title and publication_year as metadata. Cite record_id for synthetic results. PMID is null because these are fictional.

records.title: Metformin and cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes
records.abstract: This synthetic randomized, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 240 adults aged 40 to 75 years with type 2 diabetes. Participants were randomized to metformin (120 participants) or placebo (120 participants) in addition to usual care. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction and stroke at 18 months. The composite outcome occurred in 12 participants receiving metformin and 20 receiving placebo. No confidence interval or p value is reported in this abstract. Baseline cardiovascular risk and treatment adherence are not described.

records.title: Cardiovascular outcomes with metformin compared with placebo
records.abstract: In this synthetic randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 320 adults with type 2 diabetes were randomized equally to metformin or placebo alongside usual care. The primary outcome was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke during 18 months. Events occurred in 24 of 160 participants assigned metformin and 16 of 160 assigned placebo. The abstract provides no confidence interval or p value and does not describe baseline cardiovascular risk. Findings from this abstract alone do not establish the cause of the difference.

records.title: Metformin and cardiovascular events in a randomized adult diabetes trial
records.abstract: This synthetic double-blind randomized trial compared metformin with placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes. The primary endpoint was myocardial infarction or stroke. The abstract reports fewer primary events in the metformin group but does not state how many participants were randomized, the event counts, follow-up duration, confidence intervals or p values. The trial was conducted in outpatient diabetes clinics.

records.title: Earlier randomized metformin cardiovascular trial
records.abstract: This synthetic randomized trial enrolled 180 adults with type 2 diabetes and compared metformin with usual care. Ninety participants were randomized to each arm. The primary endpoint was myocardial infarction over 18 months. The abstract reports six events in the metformin arm and eight events in the usual-care arm. No confidence interval or p value is provided.

records.title: Metformin and cardiovascular injury in a mouse model
records.abstract: This synthetic laboratory experiment randomly allocated 80 mice with experimentally induced diabetes to metformin or vehicle. Investigators measured myocardial injury after an induced ischemic event. The study involved no human participants. It reports biochemical and histological outcomes and does not report human cardiovascular events.

records.title: A small randomized cardiovascular trial of metformin
records.abstract: This synthetic randomized controlled trial enrolled exactly 50 adults with type 2 diabetes: 25 were randomized to metformin and 25 to placebo. The primary endpoint was stroke during 18 months. One stroke was reported in each group. No confidence interval or p value is provided.

records.title: Metformin use and cardiovascular events in an observational cohort
records.abstract: This synthetic retrospective cohort included 600 adults with type 2 diabetes. Clinicians selected treatment as part of routine care; participants were not randomized. Investigators compared metformin users with patients receiving usual care without metformin. The endpoint was myocardial infarction or stroke identified from medical records. Adjustment for treatment-selection differences was incomplete.

records.title: Randomized metformin study of cardiovascular events
records.abstract: This synthetic randomized placebo-controlled trial enrolled 160 adults with type 2 diabetes, with 80 randomized to each arm. The primary endpoint was myocardial infarction or stroke at 12 months. Six events occurred with metformin and seven with placebo. No confidence interval or p value is reported.
